_source: SIA 263:2013, Tabelle 2 (clause 3.4.2) -- transcribed by hand from the German edition, ExternalFiles/000-Normes/SIA263-2013-DE.pdf p. 19, read off a render of the page, the table being a graphic. The only copy of these values in the project (docs/architecture/layout.md §11; one file per table or clause, named <norm>-<year>-<table or clause>-<designation>.json).
_note:
The Festigkeitsklassen of SN EN 20898-2. They belong here because a Bolzen or a Passbolzen IS a Schraube: a timber connection made with one takes its f_u from this table. A Stabdübel is not -- it is a plain round bar, whose grade is Tabelle 1's, or a fastener to SN EN 14592 carrying its own declared value, which is why f_u,k stays a field the engineer can type into whatever is chosen here.

The footnote marks the qualities SIA 263 says are not used in Switzerland (too little elongation at rupture): they are transcribed, and carried as `common: false` so that the interface can say so rather than hiding them.

⚠️ SIA 263 Tabelle 3 (Kopfbolzendübel, Gewindebolzen und Stifte, same page) is deliberately NOT transcribed. Its «Stifte» are the pins of fastenings and supports -- «Stifte für Befestigungen und Halterungen», its own Anwendungsbereich column -- and not the Stabdübel of a timber connection; offering its two rows as fastener grades would put a value in front of an engineer that does not belong to what is being calculated.
